title: Home Affairs Uniformed Services Superannuation (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Home Affairs Uniformed Services Superannuation (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Fund members and assets
sections.summary: The Fund has approximately 14,000 members and S$1.5 billion of assets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Today, the Fund has approximately 14,000 members and S$1.5 billion of assets.

sections.label: Clause 5 investment definition
sections.summary: Clause 5 expands the Act's definition of investments for more effective management of the Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 5 of the Bill will expand the definition of investments in the Act for more effective management of the Fund.

sections.label: Clause 6 Board powers
sections.summary: Clause 6 clarifies the Board's powers and functions and allows it to appoint investment managers and multiple fund managers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 6 of the Bill will clarify the scope of the Board’s powers and functions for efficient and effective governance and administration of the Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The amendments will allow the Board to appoint investment managers to construct and manage the portfolio with multiple fund managers.

sections.label: INVEST vesting and forfeiture
sections.summary: INVEST funds vest over time, but vested benefits may be reduced or terminated on dismissal with cause or conviction.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Like many private-sector deferred compensation schemes, INVEST funds vest over time, so longer service is rewarded with greater benefits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, under sections 6 and 9 of the Act, even vested benefits from the INVEST Fund may be reduced or terminated if Officers are dismissed with cause or convicted of any crime or offence.

sections.label: Protecting vested INVEST benefits
sections.summary: The speaker suggests at least a portion of vested INVEST benefits be protected from reduction or termination.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It forms an additional punishment for errant Officers that may also harm the financial security of their dependants further.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would suggest that at least a portion of the vested benefits from INVEST be protected from reduction or termination.

sections.label: Plan and CPF returns
sections.summary: The Balanced Plan returns about 4.5% and the Dynamic Plan about 5% per annum, while the Stable Plan has averaged about 2% since 2010.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Balanced Plan returns about 4.5% per annum and the Dynamic Plan about 5% per annum.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since 2010, the average annual return for the Stable Plan has been about 2% per annum compared to 2.5% for the CPF Ordinary Account.

sections.label: Automatic enrolment and default investment
sections.summary: Madrian and Shea found six in 10 automatically enrolled employees followed the default asset allocation, losing retirement benefits through inattention.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a paper titled "The Power of Suggestion: Inertia in 401(k) Participation and Savings Behaviour", published in the Quarterly Journal of Economics in 2001, Madrian and Shea studied the investment choices of employees in a large United States corporation that introduced automatic enrolment in retirement plans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They found that six out of 10 automatically enrolled employees simply followed the default asset allocation assigned by the retirement fund administrator.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is unlikely to be the optimal choice of employees in general.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is shown by the fact that among employees who made an active choice to join the retirement plan – instead of being automatically enrolled – only 1% of active choosers actually decided to allocate everything to the money market fund.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In short, six in 10 automatically enrolled employees were losing thousands of dollars in retirement benefits from investment strategies that were too conservative, not out of their choice, but because of their inattention.

sections.label: Review of INVEST Fund strategies
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to periodically review the INVEST Fund's investment strategies, officers' plan choices, and how fund administrators shape them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But we must keep up the good work.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That is why I urge the Ministry to periodically review not just the investment strategies employed by the INVEST Fund, but also the investment plan choices made by the officers, and the ways in which these are shaped by the fund administrators.

sections.label: Retirement age of uniformed officers
sections.summary: Home Affairs uniformed officers must retire at 55, ending their INVEST contributions, and the Ministry is reviewing that retirement age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Today, Home Affairs uniformed officers are required to retire at 55 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Consequently, their contributions to their INVEST account will end.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I understand that the Ministry is currently reviewing the retirement age of Home Affairs uniformed officers.

sections.label: Forfeiture of INVEST Fund monies
sections.summary: Officers dismissed after disciplinary proceedings may forfeit INVEST Fund monies, and one suggestion is pro-rating returns into the CPF Special Account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Under current regulations, officers may have their INVEST Fund monies forfeited if they are dismissed from service following a disciplinary proceeding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One suggestion is to consider pro-rating their returns and put it into the officer's CPF Special Account rather than a complete forfeiture.

sections.label: MHA review completion timeline
sections.summary: MHA is in the midst of the review, which will be completed in the next few months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: MHA is in the midst of the review which will be completed in the next few months.

sections.label: Forfeiture of superannuation benefits
sections.summary: Tax-exempt INVEST benefits can be forfeited in part or whole for dismissed errant officers, with the Public Service Commission's concurrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: INVEST benefits paid to officers on retirement are exempted from tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Therefore, if an errant officer has behaved in a manner that is unbefitting of an officer of the Home Team and is dismissed as a result of his misconduct, the superannuation benefits, in part or in whole, can and should be forfeited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The process is fair and transparent, and the forfeiture or reduction of the benefit requires the concurrence of the Public Service Commission.

sections.label: INVEST Plan investment options
sections.summary: The INVEST Plan offers three investment options, Stable, Balanced and Dynamic, which officers can choose from to suit their circumstances, needs and risk appetites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Under the INVEST Plan, there are three investment options, namely, the Stable, Balanced and Dynamic Plans and officers can choose from the three Plans to suit their personal circumstances, financial needs and appetites towards risk.

sections.label: MHA reviewing lifecycle plan
sections.summary: MHA is reviewing a lifecycle plan as a possible new investment option, seeking advice from external consultants, the INVEST Board of Trustees and its Investment Committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: MHA has been reviewing a lifecycle plan and is considering whether to introduce it as a new investment plan option for officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Advice is being sought from external consultants, the INVEST Board of Trustees and the Investment Committee of the Board, and they include members with relevant industry experience.
